items.name: Newspaper
items.condition: Dry, clean pages. No food or oil.
items.explanation: Keep clean paper dry and separate from dirty waste.
items.hint: These pages are clean and dry. Keep them with the other ordinary recyclables.

items.name: Greasy paper
items.condition: This takeaway paper is soaked with food oil.
items.explanation: Food-soiled paper belongs with residual waste in this exercise. Washing does not turn oily paper into clean paper.
items.hint: The material is paper, but its condition matters. The food oil makes the difference.

items.name: Drink bottle
items.condition: A plastic water bottle with a little water left inside.
items.readyCondition: Emptied. Clean and ready to separate.
items.preparationExplanation: The water is out. Keep the bottle separate from dirty waste and check the collector’s plastic requirements.
items.explanation: Separate clean, empty plastic bottles for recycling. Exact plastic acceptance varies by collector.
items.hint: Check inside before sorting. There is still some water to empty.

items.name: Aluminium can
items.explanation: An empty, clean aluminium can can be separated with ordinary recyclables.
items.hint: This can is already empty and clean. It does not need a special waste collection.

items.name: Used tissue
items.condition: Used to wipe up a spill. Dirty and damp.
items.explanation: Dirty tissues are residual waste, even though they began as paper.
items.hint: Being made of paper is only part of the story. This tissue is dirty.

items.name: Used battery
items.condition: An intact household battery. Not leaking or damaged.
items.explanation: Keep batteries separate and use an appropriate designated collection point. Confirm which battery types it accepts.
items.hint: Batteries need their own collection arrangements. Keep them out of ordinary recycling and residual waste.

items.name: Old phone
items.condition: An unwanted phone. Personal data has already been removed.
items.explanation: Use a collector that accepts this type of e-waste. Do not put the phone in ordinary recycling or residual waste.
items.hint: Electronics need an appropriate e-waste collection point.

items.name: Glass food jar
items.condition: An empty, clean food jar. No lid, no broken glass.
items.explanation: For this game, set glass aside for a collector that explicitly accepts food and drink containers. This is recyclable glass, not general rubbish.
items.hint: Glass can be recycled, but acceptance varies. Set it aside for a collector that specifically accepts it.
